# `Q-16-11` — Engine resolution deferred to render time

> An engine extension declares no static language claims, so Quarto
> could not decide which engine owns each document before rendering it.

## What this means

Before rendering, Quarto scans the project to work out which execution
engine owns each document. When every engine has declared its language
claims up front, that scan is a lookup — fast, and it answers for the
whole project at once.

When an engine answers only at run time, the scan cannot complete. The
documents it might own stay unresolved until the render reaches them,
and Quarto has to start the engine to find out.

The message tells you how many documents were affected:

```
Warning: engine extension `my-engine` declares no static language claims
  so engine resolution must wait for render time. Execution-language
  indexing is unavailable for 3 of 12 documents.
```

Your documents still render correctly. What is lost is the ahead-of-time
picture: features that want to know a document's execution language
without rendering it — indexing, listings, and incremental rebuild
decisions — have nothing to read for the affected documents.

## How to fix

There are two places to supply the missing information.

**In the extension** — the real fix, if you maintain it. Declare
`claims:` in its `_extension.yml`:

```yaml
contributes:
  engines:
    - path: dist/my-engine.js
      name: my-engine
      claims:
        python: true
```

See [`Q-16-10`](Q-16-10.qmd) for the full set of declarations.

**In your project** — if you do not maintain the extension, you can
answer on its behalf with a claim table under `engines:` in
`_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
engines:
  - my-engine:
      claims: [python]
```

This tells Quarto "`my-engine` handles `python`" without asking the
engine, which is enough to resolve the documents ahead of time. It is
your assertion rather than the engine's, so keep it in step with what
the engine actually does.

## When this warning does not appear

It is reported only when at least one document was actually affected. An
engine that claims at run time but that no document in your project
needs will not trigger this warning — though it will still trigger
[`Q-16-10`](Q-16-10.qmd), which is about the engine's declarations
rather than this render's outcome.
